description: A majestic hilltop fortress built with red sandstone and marble, known for its artistic Hindu style elements and the grand Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace).
history: Originally built by Raja Man Singh I in 1592 and later expanded by Sawai Jai Singh II.

description: One of the largest forts in India, situated on a high hill overlooking the blue-painted city of Jodhpur.
history: Founded around 1459 by Rao Jodha, with additions made over subsequent centuries by various rulers.

description: A massive and historically prominent fort spanning across a high hill, symbolizing Rajput valor, romance, and sacrifice.
history: Ruled by the Guhila dynasty of Mewar, it was besieged multiple times by Delhi sultans and Mughal emperors.

description: A sprawling palace complex situated along the banks of Lake Pichola, blending Rajasthani and Mughal architectural styles.
history: Started by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559 as the capital of the Mewar kingdom.

description: A group of stunning Svetambara Jain temples renowned for their extraordinary and intricate marble stone carvings.
history: Built between the 11th and 13th centuries by Vastupal and Tejpal.

description: A rare and revered 14th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Brahma, located close to the holy Pushkar Lake.
history: Believed to be over 2,000 years old, with current structures largely dating back to the 14th century.

description: A famous 20th-century temple dedicated to Karni Mata, where thousands of black rats roam freely and are considered sacred.
history: Built by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner in the early 20th century.

description: Also known as Taragarh Fort, this stunning palace complex features magnificent Bundi miniature-style mural paintings.
history: Built by Rao Raja Chattisal Singh in the 17th century.

description: A major wildlife sanctuary and tiger reserve in Sawai Madhopur, famous for its wild Bengal tigers.
history: Established as Sawai Madhopur Game Sanctuary in 1955 and declared a tiger reserve in 1973.

ticketPrices.safariBooking: Varies by zone and vehicle type

description: A renowned avian sanctuary and UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting thousands of migratory birds.
history: Created as a duck shooting reserve in the 1850s, later declared a national park in 1982.

description: A protected wildlife sanctuary and tiger reserve located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan.
history: Declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1958 and upgraded to a tiger reserve in 1978.

description: One of the largest national parks in India, located in the Thar Desert, known for desert wildlife like the Great Indian Bustard.
history: Established in 1980 to protect the unique ecosystem and fossil remains of the Thar Desert.

description: India's largest inland saltwater lake, surrounded by historical salt-producing facilities and rich birdlife.
history: Historically ruled by Chauhan kings and Mughal emperors as a major salt trading hub.

description: A sacred and picturesque freshwater lake located in the hill station of Mount Abu.
history: Associated with Hindu mythology; believed to have been dug out by the gods using their fingernails.

description: A scenic dam on the Jawai River known for its high concentration of wild leopards co-existing peacefully with local communities.
history: Built during the mid-20th century by Maharaja Umaid Singh of Jodhpur.

description: A sprawling wildlife sanctuary in the Aravalli Range known for rugged terrain, valleys, and rich flora and fauna.
history: Established in 1983 to preserve the diverse ecological zones of central Rajasthan.

description: An adventurous overnight desert camping experience under the stars atop camels in the Thar Desert.
history: A traditional mode of transport transformed into an immersive eco-tourism cultural experience.

description: An exhilarating morning aerial adventure offering panoramic bird's-eye views of Jaipur's forts, palaces, and pink city landscape.
history: A modern recreational tourism activity licensed and operated over historical zones.

description: A serene boat trip on Lake Pichola offering stunning views of Jag Mandir, the City Palace, and lakeside ghats.
history: Lake Pichola was expanded over centuries following its creation in 1362 AD.

facilities.boatJettys: City Palace jetty and Rameshwar Ghat

description: One of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs, featuring vibrant cultural performances, competitions, and religious gatherings.
history: An ancient annual traditional trading fair held in Pushkar during Kartik Shukla Ekadashi to Purnima.
